1.explanation: Link transformation for Confluence output is driven by the Confluence publish provider in TypeScript (confluence.ts and confluence-helper.ts build the pandoc call and post-process page content) together with the Lua filters under resources/extensions/quarto/confluence. The overrides.lua and publish.lua files define how Markdown link elements are rewritten into Confluence storage format links. Since the relative QMD links are not being converted to Confluence link macros, these four files are the points in the pipeline that must be modified to detect, resolve, and emit the proper Confluence link syntax for local page references.
1.bug_scenario: When publishing a Quarto site to Confluence, relative Markdown/QMD links (e.g. “* [January](2022-01.qmd)”) render correctly in local HTML but in Confluence the list items appear with no hyperlink (just bullet text). In the screenshots the local preview shows active blue links, but after Confluence publish the bullets for “January” and “March” appear as plain text with no clickable links.

2.explanation:
All of these files are part of the Quarto Confluence‐publisher plugin pipeline that takes your Markdown/Pandoc AST and turns it into Confluence storage format.  

• src/publish/confluence/confluence.ts – the main TypeScript driver that calls Pandoc, applies the Confluence Lua filters, and sends the result to Confluence.  
• src/publish/confluence/confluence-helper.ts – helper routines that build Confluence page bodies, attach metadata, and (should) transform `<a>` tags into Confluence internal‐link macros.  
• resources/extensions/quarto/confluence/publish.lua – the Lua filter invoked during `quarto publish confluence` to walk the Pandoc AST and emit Confluence‐compatible link markup.  
• resources/extensions/quarto/confluence/overrides.lua – extensions that override Quarto’s default link rendering when targeting Confluence.  

Together these components control how `[January](2022-01.qmd)` gets turned into a Confluence macro like `<ac:link><ri:page ri:content-title="2022-01"/></ac:link>`. Because the filter chain currently doesn’t detect or convert ordinary Markdown links, they get dropped (rendered as plain bullets) instead of being turned into working Confluence links.
2.bug_scenario:
A user has a simple `index.qmd` in their Quarto site that contains a bulleted list of Markdown links to other reports:

```markdown
---
title: "Reports"
---

* [January](2022-01.qmd)
* [March](2022-03.qmd)
```

When they preview the site locally (HTML output), the links render and work perfectly:

• January  
• March

However, when they run `quarto publish confluence` to push the same page to Confluence Cloud, the bullets all appear but the hyperlinks vanish:

• January  
• March

No `<a>` tags or Confluence internal‐link macros are generated, so users see plain text bullets with no clickable links.
